question.question: When a replica receives PreAccept for instance (Replica, Instance) while its local record for that instance already has Status >= ACCEPTED but stores no commands, handlePreAccept writes the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] instead of the addressed instance InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance]. Is any legal history able to put a replica in that state with preAccept.LeaderId != preAccept.Replica, and if so does the addressed record (Replica, Instance) stay without commands (halting its row's execution and the recovery replies about it) while an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) acquires a command that no quorum committed for it?
question.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).
contexts: instance owned by replica R and led by replica L != R (recovery re-proposal)
instance owned and led by the same replica (normal proposal) as the control that must behave identically
event_paths: deliver PreAccept(LeaderId=L, Replica=R, Instance=i, Ballot=b, Command=c, Seq, Deps) to a replica whose InstanceSpace[R][i] has Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil
compare the record that receives Cmds after the handler returns against the record named by (Replica, Instance)

supporting_behavior_ids.B5-slow-path-accept: shows that the accept phase stores accepted attributes on followers without any status transition, which is the premise the >= ACCEPTED branch would need
supporting_behavior_ids.B11-prepare-resolution: re-runs pre-accept on behalf of another replica's instance, which is the only read path in which PreAccept.LeaderId differs from PreAccept.Replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B12-try-preaccept: another recovery path that re-sends a command for an instance owned by a different replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B7-execute-scheduler: shows the execution requirement Cmds != nil that makes a command-less record of the addressed instance a permanent row stall

counterevidence: scoped to the writers of Instance.Cmds and Instance.Status read in this snapshot: no path sets Status >= ACCEPTED together with Cmds == nil, because the leader-side transitions copy lb.cmds in the same step (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply) and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit)

scoped to the wire format used between replicas: a nil command slice is marshalled as a zero-length prefix and unmarshalled as a non-nil empty slice, so a Commit cannot install a nil Cmds while setting COMMITTED (S13-handleCommit)

scoped to the accept path: handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps and leaves Status unchanged, so an acceptor holds no accepted status; the only records with Cmds == nil are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S14-recovery-start-prepare, S13-handleCommit)
unknowns: whether the accept phase is required to record an ACCEPTED status on the acceptor that stores accepted attributes, since the guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts and recovery sub-case 2 presuppose that some replica reports ACCEPTED

whether handlePrepareReply's value selection may adopt a reply whose Status is NONE at the highest vbal (an acceptor that stored no commands) instead of an equal-vbal reply that carries the pre-accepted value
question.trigger_rationale: Source reading showed the discrepancy directly: S9-handlePreAccept uses preAccept.Replica at lines 782, 792-798, 810, 816 and 828-829, but preAccept.LeaderId at line 809 for the same object. The state needed to reach the branch (Status >= ACCEPTED with nil Cmds on a replica receiving a PreAccept) is not produced by any path read: handleAccept stores bal/vbal/Seq/Deps without recording ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept), the leader-side ACCEPTED/COMMITTED transitions set Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), handleCommit installs commit.Command (S13-handleCommit), and a marshalled nil command slice comes back as a non-nil empty slice. The reachability premise is therefore resolved as not produced, and the separated remaining premise is whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED.

question.question: handlePreAcceptReply commits when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and inst.lb.allEqual && allCommitted && isInitialBallot, but for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty the reply-wise equality result is discarded (the allEqual accumulator is never updated), so with N = 3 the leader fast-commits its own (seq, deps) after a single reply whose recomputed attributes may differ. Can such a commit leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the fast-quorum peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which selects the reply with the highest vbal by iterating the reply slice with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, can adopt the peer's vector instead of the committed one; and does the legal crash point between the leader's local fast commit and bcastCommit make that reachable while some replica has already executed the committed vector?
question.importance: If reachable, one instance is committed with different (seq, deps) at different replicas, so the same command is ordered differently against conflicting commands on different replicas; execution then applies the same commands in different orders, the surviving replicas' state diverges, and a reply already produced under the old order is contradicted. That is a consensus-safety consequence (agreement and state-machine convergence), not a performance or liveness one.
participants: instance leader (owner of the instance row)
one fast-quorum peer that recomputed different attributes
recovering replica that later runs prepare for the instance
contexts: N = 3 with Thrifty (the configuration replica.New hardcodes and run.go passes through unchanged)
fast path with exactly FastQuorumSize-1 = 1 reply whose attributes differ from the leader's
leader crash after the local fast commit but before the Commit broadcast is delivered
event_paths: leader starts phase 1 for its own instance with deps d1/seq s1 and sends PreAccept to one peer
peer recomputes d2 != d1 (or s2 != s1) against its own conflict index and replies PREACCEPTED
leader adds the reply, skips the allEqual update because N <= 3 and Thrifty, and commits its own d1/s1, then broadcasts Commit
recoverer runs prepare and selects the candidate value among replies with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot
compare the (Seq, Deps) the recoverer re-commits with the vector the leader committed

supporting_behavior_ids.B3-preaccept-recipient: establishes the peer's differently recomputed attributes and the PREACCEPTED reply that carries them
supporting_behavior_ids.B9-recovery-trigger: shows when a leader or peer that holds an uncommitted or committed record initiates recovery of the instance
supporting_behavior_ids.B11-prepare-resolution: shows the highest-vbal selection that decides which vector is re-proposed
supporting_behavior_ids.B7-execute-scheduler: shows that execution applies the committed vector and that a reply can already have been produced before the divergence becomes visible

counterevidence: scoped to the fast-path branch: the source comment states there is no need to check equality for N <= 3 with Thrifty (S10-handlePreAcceptReply), so an author argument for the exemption may exist even though it is not written down

scoped to quorum arithmetic: for N = 3 a fast quorum of FastQuorumSize = 2 is already a majority, so the exemption may be intended to rely on fast-quorum/slow-quorum intersection instead of attribute equality (S21-quorum-sizes)

scoped to project documents: the README states that the bundled EPaxos is the corrected version and that thriftiness is required for correct recovery, which suggests the N = 3 thrifty configuration was deliberately exercised (S27-readme)
unknowns: whether a recovery-led phase 1 can leave the merged committed vector's leader-row component below the peer's record, and whether the peer's larger component can be re-committed by a recovery that reaches the peer rather than the committed leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether that requires the recovering leader to have lost its own row knowledge, which the launched configuration permits only through a restart because Durable is false and no reader of the stable store exists (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos)
question.trigger_rationale: The exemption is explicit in the source: in handlePreAcceptReply the equality result computed by mergeAttributes is only accumulated in the else branch, so for r.N <= 3 && r.Thrifty inst.lb.allEqual keeps its initial true value from newLeaderBookkeeping (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S2-instance-bookkeeping). With FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2 = 2 for N = 3 (S21-quorum-sizes) and the commit condition preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1, one disagreeing reply is enough to commit the leader's own vector. The candidate pairs the commit with the recovery rule that must reconstruct the same value: handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of the reply with the highest vbal (S15-handlePrepareReply), so two vectors at one vbal are the discriminator. A controlled multi-replica schedule is the check that could distinguish an actual same-vbal split from the author's intended majority-intersection argument.

history.question: handlePreAcceptReply commits when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and inst.lb.allEqual && allCommitted && isInitialBallot, but for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty the reply-wise equality result is discarded (the allEqual accumulator is never updated), so with N = 3 the leader fast-commits its own (seq, deps) after a single reply whose recomputed attributes may differ. Can such a commit leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the fast-quorum peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which selects the reply with the highest vbal by iterating the reply slice with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, can adopt the peer's vector instead of the committed one; and does the legal crash point between the leader's local fast commit and bcastCommit make that reachable while some replica has already executed the committed vector?
history.importance: If reachable, one instance is committed with different (seq, deps) at different replicas, so the same command is ordered differently against conflicting commands on different replicas; execution then applies the same commands in different orders, the surviving replicas' state diverges, and a reply already produced under the old order is contradicted. That is a consensus-safety consequence (agreement and state-machine convergence), not a performance or liveness one.

question.question: handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal for instance (Replica, Instance) and never writes inst.Status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept holds accepted attributes with Status NONE, and one that did see it keeps PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ. Does any decision depend on an accepted record carrying status ACCEPTED: can a later PreAccept for the same instance overwrite the accepted attributes because handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard cannot fire, and can a recovery that should re-accept an already accepted value instead take the phase-1 restart path because handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 needs a reply whose Status is ACCEPTED?
question.importance: An acceptor that stores accepted attributes without recording that it accepted them can (a) have those attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept at the same or a higher ballot instead of being preserved, and (b) hide from a recovering leader the fact that the value reached the accept phase, which is the distinction between re-proposing the accepted value and starting a fresh phase 1. Either effect can change the value a majority eventually commits for the instance, which is agreement-relevant rather than cosmetic; the accept phase is also the only place where a value is fixed without commands being stored, so a wrong reconstruction can also drop a command that only some replicas hold.

recovering replica that later runs prepare for the same instance

bindings.excerpt:
func (r *Replica) startRecoveryForInstance(replica int32, instance int32) {
	inst := r.InstanceSpace[replica][instance]
	if inst == nil {
		inst = r.newInstanceDefault(replica, instance)
		r.InstanceSpace[replica][instance] = inst
	} else if inst.Status >= COMMITTED && inst.Cmds != nil {
		r.Printf("No need to recover %d.%d", replica, instance)
		return
	}

	// no TLA guidance here (some difference with the original implementation)
	var proposals []*defs.GPropose = nil
	if inst.lb != nil {
		proposals = inst.lb.clientProposals
	}
	inst.lb = r.newLeaderBookkeepingDefault()
	lb := inst.lb
	lb.clientProposals = proposals
	lb.ballot = inst.vbal
	lb.seq = inst.Seq
	lb.cmds = inst.Cmds
	lb.deps = inst.Deps
	lb.status = inst.Status
	r.makeBallot(replica, instance)

	inst.bal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	inst.vbal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	preply := &PrepareReply{
		r.Id,
		replica,
		instance,
		inst.bal,
		inst.vbal,
		inst.Status,
		inst.Cmds,
		inst.Seq,
		inst.Deps}

	lb.prepareReplies = append(lb.prepareReplies, preply)
	lb.leaderResponded = r.Id == replica

	r.bcastPrepare(replica, instance)
}

Confirmed violation of: When Durable is enabled, recordInstanceMetadata writes the current bal, vbal, Status, Seq and Deps of an instance into the stable store; the record it produces must let each field it writes be recovered at the offset where the writer placed it, so that no value it wrote is silently replaced by another field of the same record.

Measured violation awaiting attribution: Direct-check semantic inputs changed; execution requires rechecking; Direct oracle correspondence remains disputed: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim requires that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED be adopted; the added property instead asserts that, after each replica applies the instance it holds committed, the state machines agree on the instance's key. The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.; Open review issue ef6b54abce294555b31a3c9a6ca606ac [S20-exec,S23-state-conflict-apply,S13-handleCommit,S15-handlePrepareReply,S14-recovery-start-prepare]: the accepted claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector lists execution of the instance and client-visible replies under scope.excluded, so the applied-state property tests outside the accepted proposition (claim C1 scope, S20-exec); the event is reproducible in the retained stream (applied_state_divergence with peer_value 04 and recoverer_value (void)), so the objection is about scope and attribution rather than about the observation (check 2f186bc17e13432fae3b653b42e46941)

type Replica struct {
	*replica.Replica
	prepareChan           chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptChan         chan fastrpc.Serializable
	acceptChan            chan fastrpc.Serializable
	commitChan            chan fastrpc.Serializable
	prepareReplyChan      chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptReplyChan    chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptOKChan       chan fastrpc.Serializable
	acceptReplyChan       chan fastrpc.Serializable
	tryPreAcceptChan      chan fastrpc.Serializable
	tryPreAcceptReplyChan chan fastrpc.Serializable
	prepareRPC            uint8
	prepareReplyRPC       uint8
	preAcceptRPC          uint8
	preAcceptReplyRPC     uint8
	acceptRPC             uint8
	acceptReplyRPC        uint8
	commitRPC             uint8
	tryPreAcceptRPC       uint8
	tryPreAcceptReplyRPC  uint8
	// the space of all instances (used and not yet used)
	InstanceSpace [][]*Instance
	// highest active instance numbers that this replica knows about
	crtInstance []int32
	// highest committed instance per replica that this replica knows about
	CommittedUpTo []int32
	// instance up to which all commands have been executed (including iteslf)
	ExecedUpTo       []int32
	exec             *Exec
	conflicts        []map[state.Key]*InstPair
	maxSeqPerKey     map[state.Key]int32
	maxSeq           int32
	latestCPReplica  int32
	latestCPInstance int32
	// for synchronizing when sending replies to clients
	// from multiple go-routines
	clientMutex        *sync.Mutex
	instancesToRecover chan *instanceId
	// does this replica think it is the leader
	IsLeader      bool
	maxRecvBallot int32
	batchWait     int
	transconf     bool
}

type Instance struct {
	Cmds           []state.Command
	bal, vbal      int32
	Status         int8
	Seq            int32
	Deps           []int32
	lb             *LeaderBookkeeping
	Index, Lowlink int
	bfilter        any
	proposeTime    int64
	id             *instanceId
}

type instanceId struct {
	replica  int32
	instance int32
}

type LeaderBookkeeping struct {
	clientProposals   []*defs.GPropose
	ballot            int32
	allEqual          bool
	preAcceptOKs      int
	acceptOKs         int
	nacks             int
	originalDeps      []int32
	committedDeps     []int32
	prepareReplies    []*PrepareReply
	preparing         bool
	tryingToPreAccept bool
	possibleQuorum    []bool
	tpaReps           int
	tpaAccepted       bool
	lastTriedBallot   int32
	cmds              []state.Command
	status            int8
	seq               int32
	deps              []int32
	leaderResponded   bool
}

func (r *Replica) run() {
	r.ConnectToPeers()

	r.ComputeClosestPeers()

	if r.Exec {
		go r.executeCommands()
	}

	slowClockChan = make(chan bool, 1)
	fastClockChan = make(chan bool, 1)
	go r.slowClock()

	if r.BatchingEnabled() {
		go r.fastClock()
	}

	if r.Beacon {
		go r.stopAdapting()
	}

	onOffProposeChan := r.ProposeChan

	go r.WaitForClientConnections()

	for !r.Shutdown {

		select {

		case propose := <-onOffProposeChan:
			r.handlePropose(propose)
			if r.BatchingEnabled() {
				onOffProposeChan = nil
			}
			break

		case <-fastClockChan:
			onOffProposeChan = r.ProposeChan
			break

		case prepareS := <-r.prepareChan:
			prepare := prepareS.(*Prepare)
			r.handlePrepare(prepare)
			break

		case preAcceptS := <-r.preAcceptChan:
			preAccept := preAcceptS.(*PreAccept)
			r.handlePreAccept(preAccept)
			break

		case acceptS := <-r.acceptChan:
			accept := acceptS.(*Accept)
			r.handleAccept(accept)
			break

		case commitS := <-r.commitChan:
			commit := commitS.(*Commit)
			r.handleCommit(commit)
			break

		case prepareReplyS := <-r.prepareReplyChan:
			prepareReply := prepareReplyS.(*PrepareReply)
			r.handlePrepareReply(prepareReply)
			break

		case preAcceptReplyS := <-r.preAcceptReplyChan:
			preAcceptReply := preAcceptReplyS.(*PreAcceptReply)
			r.handlePreAcceptReply(preAcceptReply)
			break

		case acceptReplyS := <-r.acceptReplyChan:
			acceptReply := acceptReplyS.(*AcceptReply)
			r.handleAcceptReply(acceptReply)
			break

		case tryPreAcceptS := <-r.tryPreAcceptChan:
			tryPreAccept := tryPreAcceptS.(*TryPreAccept)
			r.handleTryPreAccept(tryPreAccept)
			break

		case tryPreAcceptReplyS := <-r.tryPreAcceptReplyChan:
			tryPreAcceptReply := tryPreAcceptReplyS.(*TryPreAcceptReply)
			r.handleTryPreAcceptReply(tryPreAcceptReply)
			break

		case beacon := <-r.BeaconChan:
			r.ReplyBeacon(beacon)
			break

		case <-slowClockChan:
			if r.Beacon {
				r.Printf("weird %d; conflicted %d; slow %d; fast %d\n", r.Stats.M["weird"], r.Stats.M["conflicted"], r.Stats.M["slow"], r.Stats.M["fast"])
				for q := int32(0); q < int32(r.N); q++ {
					if q == r.Id {
						continue
					}
					r.SendBeacon(q)
				}
			}
			break

		case iid := <-r.instancesToRecover:
			r.startRecoveryForInstance(iid.replica, iid.instance)
		}
	}
}

func runReplica(c *config.Config, logger *dlog.Logger) {
	port := c.Port

	log.Printf("Server starting on port %d", port)
	maddr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", c.MasterAddr, c.MasterPort)
	addr := c.ReplicaAddrs[c.Alias]
	replicaId, nodeList, isLeader := registerWithMaster(addr, maddr, port)
	f := (len(c.ReplicaAddrs) - 1) / 2
	log.Printf("Tolerating %d max. failures", f)

	switch strings.ToLower(c.Protocol) {
	case "swiftpaxos":
		log.Println("Starting SwiftPaxos replica...")
		swift.MaxDescRoutines = 100
		rep := swift.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,
			c.Optread, true, false, 1, f, c, logger, nil)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "curp":
		log.Println("Starting optimized CURP replica...")
		curp.MaxDescRoutines = 100
		rep := curp.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,
			1, f, true, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "fastpaxos":
		log.Println("Starting Fast Paxos replica...")
		rep := fastpaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "n2paxos":
		log.Println("Starting N²Paxos replica...")
		rep := n2paxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, 1, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "paxos":
		log.Println("Starting Paxos replica...")
		rep := paxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, isLeader, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "epaxos":
		log.Println("Starting EPaxos replica...")
		rep := epaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, false, false, 0, false, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	}

	rpc.HandleHTTP()
	l, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf(":%d", port+1000))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal("listen error:", err)
	}
	http.Serve(l, nil)
}

SwiftPaxos: Fast Geo-Replicated State Machines
==========
<!-- [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos) -->

This repository contains the prototype implementation of SwiftPaxos, a new state-machine replication protocol for geo-distributed systems.
SwiftPaxos is a _faster Paxos without compromises_.
In the best case, it executes a state-machine command in two message delays (one round-trip), and three otherwise.
SwiftPaxos was [presented](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) at the 21st USENIX Symposium on Networked Systems Design and Implementation ([NSDI '24](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24)).

Installation
------------

    git clone https://github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos.git
    cd swiftpaxos
    go install github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos

Implemented protocols
---------------------

|  Protocol               | Comments                                          |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| SwiftPaxos              | See our NSDI'24 [paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) for the full details.|
| Paxos                   | The classic Paxos protocol.                       |
| N<sup>2</sup>Paxos      | All-to-all variant of Paxos.                      |
| CURP                    | CURP implemented over N<sup>2</sup>Paxos.         |
| Fast Paxos              | Fast Paxos with uncoordinated collision recovery. |
| EPaxos                  | A [corrected][epaxos_correct] version of EPaxos.  |

This software is based on the [Egalitarian Paxos](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos) code base, as well as the corrections made [here](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos).

Usage
-----
#### participants
There are three types of participants: *master*, *servers* and *clients*. 
The servers and clients implement the protocol logic. 
The master maintains the configuration of the system.

#### deployment configuration
To setup a run, the participants read deployment configuration file. 
See [aws.conf][config] for an example of configuration file for AWS EC2.

#### launching a participant

Master:
    
    swiftpaxos -run master -config conf.conf

Server:

    swiftpaxos -run server -config conf.conf -alias server_name

Client:

    swiftpaxos -run client -config conf.conf -alias client_name

#### command line options

    -alias alias
        An alias of this participant
    -config file

runTime:     none // 5min
writes:      100
conflicts:   2
commandSize: 1000
clones:      99
key:         42 // conflicting key

audit_question.question: When Durable is enabled, recordInstanceMetadata writes the current bal, vbal, Status, Seq and Deps of an instance into the stable store. Does the record it produces preserve the value written for bal at the offset where the recorder wrote it, or does a later write of the same record replace it, and does Status land inside the bytes a reader would use for vbal?
audit_question.importance: A record that cannot carry the fields the writer intended hides the ballot context of an instance from any reader of that layout (a recovery path or an external tool), so a replica that restarts from such a record would be missing the value it needs to compare ballots. The consequence is bounded here because the shipped configuration passes durable=false and no reader exists in the snapshot, which is why this is recorded as an implementation-semantics defect rather than a live availability or agreement failure.

Bounded direct comparison completed; local attribution remains pending: Direct oracle correspondence remains disputed: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim requires that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED be adopted; the added property instead asserts that, after each replica applies the instance it holds committed, the state machines agree on the instance's key. The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.; Open review issue ef6b54abce294555b31a3c9a6ca606ac [S20-exec,S23-state-conflict-apply,S13-handleCommit,S15-handlePrepareReply,S14-recovery-start-prepare]: the accepted claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector lists execution of the instance and client-visible replies under scope.excluded, so the applied-state property tests outside the accepted proposition (claim C1 scope, S20-exec); the event is reproducible in the retained stream (applied_state_divergence with peer_value 04 and recoverer_value (void)), so the objection is about scope and attribution rather than about the observation (check 2f186bc17e13432fae3b653b42e46941)

grounding.derivation: Recovery exists to carry the value that could have been committed across a change of leader. In this snapshot the recovering replica seeds its bookkeeping from its own record, makes a new ballot and reports that new ballot as its own VBallot, while handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of a reply only when element.VBallot >= the running lb.ballot. The responsibility asserted here is that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED must be adopted, because a committed record is the authoritative value for that instance and is the only input that can keep the recovering replica consistent with replicas that already installed the commit.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the captured snapshot with N=3 and Thrifty, IsLeader false, the recovering replica holding a default NONE record for the instance and one slow-quorum peer holding a COMMITTED record with a command; the recovery is entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance.
unresolved: whether a full legal history (real proposal, accept round, commit broadcast, execution timeout) reaches the same state
whether the launched configuration permits a replica to hold a default record for an instance that another replica has committed
alternatives: an alternative reading is that the recovering replica is only required to adopt the value with the highest vbal and that the local record's new ballot legitimately outranks an older committed vbal, which the review should test against the cited resolution code

before.old_judgment: The C1 obligation's scope excluded execution but did not say where the applied-state consequence belongs, which let an artifact assert it under C1.

after.new_judgment: The C1 obligation ends at adopting the reported committed vector; applied-state agreement for a committed instance is claim C3's proposition, and the scope now says so explicitly.

grounding.derivation: The boundary follows the two obligations already accepted: C1's properties concern the value a recovery adopts, and C3's concern the effect replicas apply from the committed vector, which the executor and state application establish.

selections.rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The map is sourced only from the captured snapshot; all anomalies found while tracing the backbone are retained as open_details instead of being asserted as defects. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

after.purpose: Form a per-instance decision: fix the command, its sequence number and its dependency vector, and advance the instance from tentative pre-accept through accept to commit.
after.realization_summary: handlePropose allocates (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq,deps) from the local conflict tables, records the instance as PREACCEPTED and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers (Thrifty). handlePreAccept recomputes attributes on the receiver and replies with (bal,vbal,seq,deps,CommittedUpTo,status). handlePreAcceptReply merges replies and commits on the fast path when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and allEqual and (for N>7) allCommitted and the ballot is the initial ballot; otherwise the instance moves to ACCEPTED and a majority accept round runs in handleAcceptReply (acceptOKs+1 > N/2), followed by bcastCommit.
variants: Thrifty fast quorum versus full broadcast
N<=3 and Thrifty skip the attribute-equality check
N>7 propagates committedDeps and can make the fast path fail on allCommitted
batching when batchWait > 0 (disabled by run.go)
unknowns: whether skipping the equality check for N<=3 with Thrifty is compensated by another mechanism

after.purpose: Carry the per-instance authority context: which ballot the record is promised to, at which ballot its attributes were last fixed, and which replica may currently advance it.
after.realization_summary: Each Instance keeps bal (highest ballot promised) and vbal (ballot at which the current attributes were established). maxRecvBallot is raised by every received message type and constrains makeBallot, which picks id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and further raised while IsLeader. Ballot comparison gates every message and reply: lower ballots are dropped or nacked, and a majority of nacks lets a replica raise the ballot and run prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead it does.

recovery ballot for a non-owner is shifted by N
unknowns: whether any in-repository caller other than a nack majority ever sets IsLeader

after.purpose: Re-establish eligible participation for an instance that is blocking execution by reconstructing its attributes and value from a majority.
after.realization_summary: executeCommands times out an instance that has stayed uncommittable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (10s) and pushes instancesToRecover; startRecoveryForInstance returns early when the local record is already committed with commands, otherwise it seeds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record and broadcasts Prepare. handlePrepareReply waits for SlowQuorumSize replies at the current ballot, takes the attributes of the highest vbal and selects sub-case 1..6 (already committed, accepted, pre-accepted with enough equal support, weaker pre-accepted support, restart phase 1 with the recovered or NOOP command).

after.purpose: Define participant eligibility and quorum arithmetic: who is a member, who is believed alive, and how many equal or majority supports are needed.
after.realization_summary: N and F come from the peer address list and the master-visible participant count; FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2, SlowQuorumSize = (N+1)/2, WriteQuorumSize = F+1, ReadQuorumSize = N-F. Alive[] is set during connection setup and cleared by replicaListener when a peer reader fails; PreferredPeerOrder (from ComputeClosestPeers or the latency table) decides which FastQuorumSize-1 peers and which majority peers receive PreAccept/Accept/Commit.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

selections.rationale: Source review resolved the Candidate's discriminator without needing execution. The wrong-slot write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 assigns the received command to InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance], but every other access in handlePreAccept addresses the instance named by the message, (preAccept.Replica, preAccept.Instance). The premise that branch needs -- a local record with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil -- is not produced by any status-advancing path in the snapshot: handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but leaves Status at NONE; the leader-side accept and commit transitions (handlePreAcceptReply, handleTryPreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply) copy lb.cmds and set the command in the same step as the status; handleCommit copies commit.Command, which arrives through the wire format where a nil slice is unmarshalled as a non-nil empty slice; and the only records with nil Cmds are freshly created defaults with Status NONE. The map is updated in the same product: Behaviors B3 and B5 record the sourced protection and the answered unknown, and core_overview's first open detail is replaced by the sourced conditional relationship. feedback.answered: The Candidate's discriminator is resolved on sources: no legal history in the captured snapshot establishes the branch premise. A replica that receives PreAccept can hold Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil only if some local transition sets ACCEPTED, COMMITTED or EXECUTED without also installing commands. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE even though it holds accepted attributes (S11-handleAccept). Every transition that does set Status >= ACCEPTED also sets Cmds in the same handler: handlePreAccept stores the received command when it sets PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ (S9-handlePreAccept), the leader-side accept and commit paths set inst.Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit). A commit command cannot arrive as nil through the wire format: Marshal writes a zero-length prefix and Unmarshal allocates a non-nil empty slice. The only nil-Cmds records are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S13-handleCommit, S14-recovery-start-prepare). whether the intended acceptor status semantics are external to this snapshot (the corrected EPaxos specification or reference implementation) rather than inferable from in-repository callers

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.
